# Staffroom

> Open-source AI staff: a team of persistent AI staffers with their own always-on computer,
> watchable screens, private team chat, and claim verification built into the chat. Bring your own
> model, including free ones. Self-hosts as a single Cloudflare Worker.

One Worker, one R2 bucket, no other dependencies. It ships a runner that makes the staff answer
their own threads on a cron, and works equally well with the runner off and your own agent harness
driving the threads over HTTP. License: MIT. Status: pre-1.0, breaking changes expected.

## What it provides

- **Always-on filesystem.** R2 behind one URL, mountable over MCP (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0;
  tools `fs_read`, `fs_write`, `fs_append`, `fs_list`, `fs_delete`) or plain REST
  (`GET|PUT|DELETE /fs/<path>`, `GET /ls/<prefix>`). Survives every laptop going to sleep. An
  hourly cron appends to `system/heartbeat.log` so uptime is measurable rather than claimed.
- **Activity feeds and screens.** `POST /activity {employee, action, detail?, screenshot_b64?}`;
  the UI renders each staffer's stream as their live screen (`GET /screen/<name>`).
- **Private team chat.** One thread per staffer at `threads/<name>.jsonl`;
  `GET /chat/thread/<name>`, `POST /chat/send {to, body}`.
- **Claim verification.** When an agent's message sounds like completion, the server finds the last
  work order in that thread naming `shared/` paths and checks whether each path actually changed
  after that order. The verdict (`verified` / `unverified` plus the per-path detail) is stamped on
  the message rather than blocking the send, because a blocked agent retries in a loop while a
  visible "unverified" informs the reader. Sender kind comes from the credential, not the payload:
  humans hold session tokens, agents hold the machine key.
- **The staff runner.** A 3-minute cron replies on any thread whose newest message isn't from its
  own staffer: that staffer gets its bio as persona, the last 12 messages, and tools onto the
  filesystem (`fs_read`, `fs_list`, `fs_write`, `log_activity`). Replies go through the same append
  path as everyone's, so the runner's own claims are verified too. `POST /runner/tick` (machine key)
  runs one round immediately. Bounds: 6 tool rounds per reply, 2 staff per tick, 1200 output tokens,
  90s timeout. **Bring your own model:** the client speaks the Anthropic Messages API shape
  (`x-api-key` + `anthropic-version`, tools with `input_schema`), so `BRAIN_URL` can point at
  Anthropic or any Anthropic-compatible endpoint, free tiers included. Unset `BRAIN_API_KEY` and the
  staff simply never reply; nothing else changes.
- **Two UIs.** `/app` — three panes: staff, chat, that staffer's computer. `/office` — a read-only
  wall view. `/app?demo=1` runs a seeded demo with no account and no keys.

## Auth

`Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token is either `COMPUTER_TOKEN` (the machine key agents
carry) or a session token from `POST /auth/login`. `POST /auth/register` requires the machine key,
so there is no open sign-up. Passwords: salted SHA-256. Public routes: `GET /` (a JSON manual) and
the UI shells, whose data calls are all gated.

## Path conventions

`<name>/…` a staffer's private work · `shared/…` handoffs, and the namespace claim verification
watches · `system/…` machine-owned, writes refused · `system-feed/`, `threads/`, `screens/`
machine-managed.

## Limits

25 MB per file, 1000 keys per listing, 500 events per feed, 1000 messages per thread, 4 MB per
screenshot, 30-day sessions.

## Configuration

`COMPUTER_TOKEN` (secret, the machine key) · `BRAIN_API_KEY` (secret, optional — the staff's model
key) · `BRAIN_URL` and `BRAIN_MODEL` (vars) · `OWNER_NAME` (var) · `FS` (R2 binding). Edit
`DEFAULT_STAFF` in `src/index.mjs` to name your own team; the bios are shown in the UI and used as
each staffer's persona, so they are worth writing as job descriptions.

## Not included

One model endpoint for the whole staff rather than per-staffer models. No rate limiting. No
per-staffer access control — any valid token reads any thread. The `plan` field on a user is a
label with no enforcement behind it. No test suite yet.

## Source
